lines:
Separate topic split out of #172. Lower priority. Skills are **not** plugins — a skill is procedural knowledge, not a capability.

## Current state

Aworkit already implements the skill **runtime**: portable `SKILL.md` (YAML `name` + `description` + markdown body), discovery precedence (`.aworkit/skills`, `.agents/skills`, configured absolute folders, `~/.aworkit/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, optional bundled folder), the `tool.skill` binding, a `skill` model tool with `<skill_content>` wrappers and progressive catalog scanning, and a `/name` user gesture that loads a user-invocable skill once. See `docs/skills-and-memory.md`.

## Gap

The product surface around skills is thin: there is no first-class way to install/manage skills, see what was discovered and what was rejected, refresh discovery, or invoke a skill with an obvious gesture. Codex uses `$`/`/skills`, ChatGPT uses `@`; Aworkit currently uses `/name`.

## Deliverables

1. **Skills management surface**: list discovered skills with name/description/source folder; show malformed/duplicate/rejected entries and why; show which root each came from.
2. **Install/import**: bring a skill folder in from an external location (copy into a chosen skills root), and an **Open skills folder** action; a **Refresh** action.
3. **Invocation**: a clear, discoverable gesture in the composer (keep `/name`, consider an `@`-style picker) that lists available user-invocable skills; respect `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable` controls.
4. **Configuration**: expose the additional absolute skill folders, bundled folder, and default-discovery toggle with plain-language labels.
5. **Docs**: extend the skills documentation into user-facing guidance and an agent-facing authoring skill.

## Out of scope

Plugin packaging/configuration (that is #172). Skills do not gain runtime capabilities; helper scripts continue to run through the agent's existing authorized tools.

## Acceptance criteria

- A skill dropped into a skills root is discovered after Refresh and shows its name/description/source.
- A malformed skill is reported with a reason instead of silently skipped.
- A user can invoke a listed skill from the composer and see it applied once to that input.
- Model-only and user-only invocation controls are respected.
- No user-facing jargon; labels are understandable without knowing the skill file format.

data.title: Skills: install/manage surface and clear invocation gesture for the existing SKILL.md system (lower priority)
